program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding deep passes; consolidate and run heavy validation after Wave 2500

source_provenance: Direct PubMed/NCBI discovery and sequential abstract verification
PMID-level dedupe against cumulative Wave 2075 deep selection

waves.title: Effects of Curcumin/Turmeric Supplementation on Kidney Function in Individuals With Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomised Controlled Trials.
waves.finding: Curcumin/turmeric supplementation significantly reduced urea but did not significantly change creatinine, BUN, uric acid, or albumin; a creatinine publication-bias signal was detected.
waves.safety: Evidence certainty ranged from moderate to low and does not establish broad renoprotection.

waves.title: Efficacy and Safety of Probiotic Supplementation for Neonatal Jaundice: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
waves.population: preterm and full-term neonates with jaundice
waves.finding: Probiotic supplementation reduced bilirubin at several early time points and shortened phototherapy and hospital duration in pooled analyses.
waves.safety: Neonatal, short-term evidence requires strain- and population-specific interpretation; long-term efficacy and safety remain uncertain.

waves.title: Vitamin D supplementation for prevention of vitamin D deficiency in preterm and low birth weight infants.
waves.finding: Vitamin D supplementation reduced deficiency risk; higher versus lower dosing further reduced deficiency but did not clearly improve osteopenia or bone mineral content.
waves.safety: Higher-dose regimens probably increased vitamin-D excess, creating a clear dose-safety tradeoff in a vulnerable population.

waves.title: Dietary Magnesium Intake in Relation to Depression in Adults: A GRADE-Assessed Systematic Review and Dose-Response Meta-analysis of Epidemiologic Studies.
waves.study: systematic review/dose-response meta-analysis of observational studies; 63,214 participants
waves.population: adults in cohort and cross-sectional studies
waves.finding: Higher dietary magnesium intake was associated with lower depression risk, with an inverse dose-response pattern across observational data.
waves.safety: Association does not establish antidepressant efficacy of magnesium supplements and remains vulnerable to dietary and lifestyle confounding.

waves.title: Curcumin Versus Corticosteroids for Symptomatic Oral Lichen Planus: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.study: systematic review of 11 clinical trials; 499 patients
waves.population: people with symptomatic oral lichen planus
waves.finding: Curcumin reduced pain more than corticosteroids at one week, but later pain outcomes and clinical lesion improvement were generally comparable.
waves.safety: High risk of bias and substantial heterogeneity weaken conclusions; delivery formulations and comparator regimens varied.

waves.title: Evaluation of glycine treatment for reducing alcohol craving and self-administration in individuals with alcohol use disorder: A human laboratory trial.
waves.population: 48 adults with alcohol use disorder completing an alcohol self-administration challenge
waves.finding: Five days of oral glycine raised serum glycine but did not reduce alcohol craving, laboratory alcohol consumption, or most subjective alcohol effects versus placebo.
waves.safety: Direct human null evidence does not support glycine as a stand-alone anti-craving treatment; exploratory craving–consumption dissociation requires replication.

waves.title: The Impact of Metformin on Vitamin B12 Levels in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Single-Arm Meta-Analysis.
waves.finding: Vitamin B12 levels declined numerically after 6 and 12 months of metformin, but changes were neither statistically nor clinically significant; deficiency estimates differed greatly between RCT and observational data.
waves.safety: Evidence is sparse and heterogeneous; this informs monitoring risk rather than vitamin-B12 supplementation efficacy.

waves.title: Vitamin D supplementation in infertile men: a systematic review and meta-analysis of effects on semen quality and endocrine function.
waves.finding: Oral vitamin D was associated with small improvements in semen volume, sperm concentration, progressive motility, and testosterone, but not clinical pregnancy or live birth.
waves.safety: Adverse-event reporting was limited; surrogate semen improvements do not establish improved fertility outcomes, and higher doses did not show added benefit.

waves.title: Vitamin D Pretreatment to Prevent the Risk of Postoperative Hypocalcemic Complications After Parathyroidectomy in Primary Hyperparathyroidism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: people with primary hyperparathyroidism undergoing parathyroidectomy
waves.finding: Preoperative vitamin D was associated with lower postoperative and symptomatic hypocalcemia and a modestly shorter hospital stay.
waves.safety: Overall evidence quality was low; this is perioperative treatment-context evidence, not general supplementation guidance.

waves.title: Consuming grass finished lamb improves blood plasma ω-3 fatty acid response among healthy consumers.
waves.finding: Eating grass-finished versus concentrate-finished lamb increased several plasma omega-3 fatty acids over four weeks, without differences in measured cardiovascular risk factors.
waves.safety: This is a whole-food matrix intervention and should not be treated as evidence for omega-3 supplement efficacy.

waves.title: The Route of Administration Determines the Efficacy of Zinc in Preventing Radiation-Induced Oral Mucositis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.finding: Overall zinc reduced severe oral-mucositis risk, but route analysis showed the signal was driven by topical mouthwash; systemic oral zinc produced borderline, inconsistent benefit.
waves.safety: The authors explicitly conclude oral systemic zinc does not provide reliable prophylactic benefit; topical results remain hypothesis-generating due to very limited trials.

waves.title: Comprehensive PRISMA Based Systematic Review: Exploring the Phytochemistry, Pharmacological Profile and Clinical aspects of Panax ginseng.
waves.study: broad systematic review spanning phytochemistry, preclinical pharmacology, and clinical literature
waves.finding: The review catalogued ginsenosides and other constituents alongside broad anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, metabolic, and anticancer mechanisms, but did not provide a focused high-certainty clinical efficacy synthesis.
waves.safety: Broad mechanistic reviews are useful for identity and mechanism mapping but should not be promoted as proof of clinical benefit.

waves.title: Nutrition and dietary supplements in age-related macular degeneration.
waves.study: narrative review of epidemiology, clinical trials, and experimental evidence
waves.population: people at risk for or living with age-related macular degeneration
waves.finding: Defined AREDS-style supplementation has evidence for reducing progression from intermediate to late AMD, while broader nutrient and dietary associations remain more mixed.
waves.safety: Benefits apply to specific AMD risk groups and formulations, not indiscriminate use of lutein, zinc, omega-3, or other nutrients in the general population.

waves.title: Interactions Between Nutraceuticals and α-Synuclein Conformational States: Molecular Mechanisms and Neuroprotective Implications in Parkinson's Disease.
waves.finding: Multiple dietary bioactives can interfere with alpha-synuclein aggregation or clearance in experimental systems.
waves.safety: Poor bioavailability, blood-brain-barrier limitations, and overwhelmingly preclinical evidence prevent clinical neuroprotection claims.

waves.title: EFFICACY OF MELATONIN AS AN ADJUNCT TO NONSURGICAL PERIODONTAL THERAPY: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS.
waves.finding: Adjunctive melatonin improved some attachment, pocket-depth, gingival, plaque, and short-term glycemic outcomes at selected time points.
waves.safety: Prediction intervals crossed the null for key periodontal outcomes and heterogeneity was substantial, so consistent clinical benefit is uncertain.

waves.title: Therapeutic Effects of Probiotics on Symptoms of Anxiety in Children and Adolescents: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Placebo-Controlled Trials.
waves.finding: Probiotics did not significantly improve anxiety overall; subgroup benefit appeared in neurodevelopmental disorders, especially autism, but was based on only a few trials.
waves.safety: Sparse subgroup evidence and strain/population heterogeneity preclude a general pediatric anxiolytic claim.

waves.title: The effects of protein supplementation on body composition after bariatric surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.finding: Protein supplementation modestly improved weight, muscle mass, fat-free mass, and fat mass, but did not significantly change BMI or lean body mass.
waves.safety: Certainty was moderate to low and findings are surgery-specific; the review itself judged evidence insufficient for firm recommendations.

waves.title: The Role of Omega-3 Polyunsaturated Fatty Acid Supplementation in Postoperative Recovery of Colorectal Cancer: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.finding: Omega-3 interventions improved several nutritional, immune, inflammatory, and postoperative recovery measures and shortened hospitalization, but did not improve mortality.
waves.safety: Clinical nutrition regimens and oncology context limit translation to routine supplement use; post-hoc dose-response estimates are not consumer dosing guidance.

waves.title: Probiotics and aging: Impacts on cognitive function, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, inflammation, and antioxidant activity. A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of probiotic trials in adults age 50+
waves.population: older adults, including cognitively impaired populations
waves.finding: Probiotics showed modest cognitive improvements and changes in several BDNF, inflammatory, and oxidative-stress markers.
waves.safety: Substantial heterogeneity and limited biomarker evidence reduce certainty; multi-strain apparent advantages are not proof of class-wide efficacy.

waves.title: Resistance training combined with creatine supplementation: a three-level meta-analysis of multidimensional outcomes from strength enhancement to body composition remodeling.
waves.finding: Creatine plus resistance training improved upper- and lower-body strength and lean mass versus resistance training alone, with a small rise in body mass and small reduction in body-fat percentage; fat mass itself was not significantly different.
waves.safety: Moderator findings, including larger strength effects in younger groups, were exploratory; diet and training backgrounds were heterogeneously reported.

waves.title: Effects of Probiotic and Synbiotic Supplementation on Metabolic and Hepatic Outcomes in Children and Adolescents With Obesity, Including Those With Obesity-Related Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: children and adolescents with obesity or obesity-related MASLD
waves.finding: Probiotic/synbiotic supplementation reduced total cholesterol, LDL-C, and ALT, but did not improve BMI-z, waist circumference, triglycerides, HDL-C, or fasting glucose; HOMA-IR increased.
waves.safety: Mixed metabolic effects, substantial heterogeneity, and low/very-low certainty for many outcomes require caution.

waves.title: Meta-analysis of the Effects of Probiotics on Alcoholic Liver Disease.
waves.population: people with alcoholic fatty liver, alcoholic hepatitis, or cirrhosis
waves.finding: Probiotics reduced ALT and produced a borderline AST reduction, but did not significantly improve bilirubin, albumin, or GGT.
waves.safety: Liver-disease stage, geography, strains, and treatment duration varied; enzyme changes do not establish improved clinical outcomes.

waves.title: The mechanism of probiotics in pregnancy outcomes in overweight or obese pregnant women based on meta-analysis, network pharmacology and molecular docking.
waves.study: meta-analysis of 8 RCTs plus network-pharmacology/molecular-docking analyses
waves.finding: Probiotics did not significantly improve adverse pregnancy outcomes overall; a subgroup using Bifidobacterium plus Lactobacillus showed reduced small-for-gestational-age risk.
waves.safety: The positive subgroup is hypothesis-generating, and computational mechanism work does not validate clinical efficacy.

waves.title: An updated systematic review and appraisal of the pathophysiologic mechanisms of probiotics in alleviating depression.
waves.population: people with depressive symptoms or depression
waves.finding: Probiotics produced a modest pooled reduction in depressive symptoms, with substantial heterogeneity and stronger signals reported for certain strains or multi-strain products.
waves.safety: Strain-specific findings and heterogeneous scales/mechanisms prevent generalizing benefit to all probiotic products.

waves.title: Topical curcumin in the treatment of denture stomatitis: a systematic review of clinical efficacy.
waves.study: systematic review of 5 randomized clinical trials; 207 participants
waves.finding: Topical curcumin delivered as mouthwash, ointment, or photodynamic solution reduced Candida albicans colony counts and clinical signs across included trials.
waves.safety: Evidence quality was moderate with inconsistency and risk of bias; topical delivery findings do not establish oral curcumin supplement efficacy.
